newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads widen on new supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads widen on new supply.

text.p: Investment-grade corporate bond prices began to show signs of strain as more than $1 billion in new supply poured into the U.S. market for the second day in a row, traders said.
By the close of trading on Thursday, spreads on investment-grade bonds had widened by roughly five basis points across the board, they said.
Traders said the spread widening was due to investors selling their old bonds to finance purchases of the new product being offered.
Bonds in the bank and finance sector performed especially poorly as investors continued to express a preference for a new type of preferred stock being issued by banks.
"They must have done a real dog and poney show to sell this stuff," said one amazed trader.
"We have people involved in these preferreds that would not even buy bank paper previously."
The trader speculated that bank paper is currently oversold and that spreads may tighten in the sector over the next several days.
Unlike in high-grade, prices in the junk market held firm relatively to Treasuries in the face of a flood of new deals.
Energy sector bonds continued see strong bids as a result of investor perceptions that oil prices are trending higher.
The positive sentiment boosted a 144a junk offering by HS Resources Inc, an oil exploration and production company that price on Thursday via Salomon Brothers Inc.

The deal was upsized to $150 million from 125 million as a result of strong investor demand. It was priced at 320 basis points over Treasuries, compared with price talk which had targeted a 325 basis point spread.
In addition to the sheer number of new deals, Thursday was notable for some of the more unique transactions to hit the market:

-Enersis SA, a Chilean electricity company, debuted in the U.S. debt market with a $800 million deal through J.P. Morgan & Co. The deal was upsized from $500 million due to strong demand, sources said.
-Newport News Shipbuilding and Drydock Co, became the first American shipbuilding company to issue junk bonds by selling $400 million in notes through J.P. Morgan
-Circus Circus Enterprises, a Las Vegas-based casino, sold $150 milllion in 100-year bonds via Morgan Stanley & Co and $150 million in 40-year bonds and Goldman Sachs & Co.
